label: conformance over tested domain, not universal correctness
notes: The reference is the erf/tanh form x*0.5*(1+f(.)) with a correctly rounded f (F32ErfRn/F32TanhRn); torch uses the same formula on two code paths. (i) Strided tensors -> scalar libm std::erf/std::tanh: erf form 98.8% of f32 words exact (glibc erff is not correctly rounded everywhere), tanh form 93.6%. (ii) Contiguous tensors (all bf16, f32) -> ATen Vectorized<float>::erf/tanh: the vectorised erf is a polynomial approximation with absolute error up to ~3.5e-7 near x=0 (worst tested word x=-0.03167: 8 ulps of the result) and is NOT the same erf as torch.erf on a contiguous tensor (MKL VML vsErf, <= 1 ulp: see the F32ErfRn_v1 record; probe: F.gelu(x) != x*0.5*(1+torch.erf(x*M_SQRT1_2)) at x=-1.0); the vectorised tanh is Sleef <= 1 ulp (tanh(-9.009) = -1.0 where correctly rounded is -0.99999994). For x < 0 the 1+f cancellation amplifies f's error (2 ulps at x=-1; factor-2 or -0.0-vs-1.6e-7 results for x < -5), which is why the f32 exact fraction is low while the absolute difference stays within 0.5*|x|*2^-21 + 4 ulp on every path. bf16 outputs absorb all of it but 3 (erf) / 4 (tanh, the tail -0.0) words of the exhaustive 65,280.

oracle.op: torch.nn.functional.gelu(approximate='tanh') on a contiguous (vectorised) and a strided (scalar) tensor

torch_scalar_path_strided.tolerance: 0.5*|x|*2^-21 + 4*ulp_DT(ref)   (oracle's erf/tanh within 4.8e-7 absolute of correctly rounded; measured worst 3.5e-7)

torch_vectorised_path_contiguous.tolerance: 0.5*|x|*2^-21 + 4*ulp_DT(ref)   (oracle's erf/tanh within 4.8e-7 absolute of correctly rounded; measured worst 3.5e-7)
